title: Compile the exact minimum Gaussian queries over ordinary involution sectors
body:
This emits an **optimal dyadic query word** for A(J)+B(J)Q over a finite Boolean family of ordinary involutions. The minimum is max over sectors of rank(B_sector), even with interleaved queries, retained results and feedback in the stated alphabet. A verified 32-sector invertible example uses one query instead of 32 separate sector queries; its 2080 shifted ADDs, 34 CLEARs and 33 owned fields are explicit. No new kappa is claimed.

[Scope](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/380591a21cad88c03a05a8e8177ed0eede85c492/research/optimal-sector-query-compiler/README.md), [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/380591a21cad88c03a05a8e8177ed0eede85c492/research/optimal-sector-query-compiler/PROOF.md), [exact checks](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/380591a21cad88c03a05a8e8177ed0eede85c492/research/optimal-sector-query-compiler/verify.py), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/380591a21cad88c03a05a8e8177ed0eede85c492/research/optimal-sector-query-compiler/SOURCES.json), [registered replay](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/380591a21cad88c03a05a8e8177ed0eede85c492/research/optimal-sector-query-compiler/VERIFY.json). Base: canonical main `6cf7a683f447b9f1e2333791907fd92be5009a63`, priority revision 7. Contribution head: `380591a21cad88c03a05a8e8177ed0eede85c492`.

This extends PR5578 T6 with an exact compiler, arbitrary finite Boolean sector families and a matching lower bound. The usual lifted central Gaussian with independent spectator translations meets the faithful-sector condition at every width f>=3. It also proves the scalar role-gauge tariff rank(RM-MP) is already exact in this alphabet, so sector packing cannot lower that boundary without a changed premise. [Discussion5623](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5623) coordinates the PR5586 C8 enabling work.

Normal and optimized registered replay pass. A separate formal interpreter checks every original and dirty-owned column for all 6561 small sector-matrix pairs, 72 rectangular cases, 72 noncoordinate role-gauge boundaries and 160 feedback words. Independent rational rank checks certify the count. Sixty basis cases use literal tensor Gaussian matrices at widths 1-4. Four input or word corruption controls reject. The source two-sector example is retained and credited; its emitted word SHA256 is 668b6303a9526fe613b154aeae45e5082fa39be3431c1aeb57c96d3488d89891.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/optimal-sector-query-compiler
```

Python 3.12 and the standard library suffice. Committed-byte checks pass. The minimum requires nonzero sectors on which I and Q are independent, scalar combinations of the declared ordinary involutions, and one-field Q/Q-inverse queries. Other address maps and higher-rank Gaussian requests are outside it. No actual caller section has been replaced and no new Gaussian targets are credited. Native movement, coefficient implementation, precision, full compiler/outer funding, formal-kernel and independent scientific acceptance remain open. Full historical ancestry was not rerun. Hosted status is unconfirmed at publication.

Credit Dugongue PR5578 T3/T6/T7 and PR5586 C8. The exact Smith utility is retained from Ali Romman PR5615 head d914f77d948ac377bdb9823daca93d08913c3fa7, with byte authentication before execution and exact factor checks. Credit Nick Petalas for prior Euclidean methods, and Cao Yifan, DaysSky, Cinna Davis, Ryanson Jonathan, zxv, Jacob Alan Sussman and all retained native/controller/compiler authors.

Next: extract an actual caller section on a lawful snapshot and compare the emitted query and ordinary bill. The selected frontier is unchanged.
